findings.message: The Summary block restates the upstream design intent for the whole track in prose instead of keeping the text to target + operation + anchor cite.
S1 restates the semantic-verdict migration contract in prose; T001/T002 should be described only as target + operation + anchor cite per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.
S2 restates the rules/config behavior contract in prose, including the default config contents; T003-T005 should stay at target + operation + anchor cite.
S3 restates the domain-model contract in prose instead of limiting itself to executable task text.
S4 restates the codec behavior contract in prose; the section should not re-explain the serialization guarantees.
S5 restates the scanner/verifier behavior contract in prose; T013-T015 should avoid re-describing the upstream semantics.
S6 restates the derive/check/evaluate/results contracts in prose, including deterministic projection, totality, cache freezing, and aggregation semantics.
S7 restates the CLI wiring contract in prose; T020-T022 should be trimmed to target + operation + anchor cite.
S8 restates the capability-registration contract in prose instead of keeping the section to the executable change description.
T006's contract attributes `RoleName` and `DiagnosticMessage`, but the task text only scopes hashes/ids plus `WaivedReason`; that attribution is broader than the described work.

T005 restates ADR D13 content (`data_roles (17), contract_roles (4), function_roles (2), patterns.typestate, trait_impls sections`) instead of keeping the task to target + operation + anchor cite; this violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

S3 (T006-T008) embeds upstream behavior prose (`deterministic from identity fields only`, `cache-key triple invalidates verdict`, `six variants`) rather than just executable task directives; strip the contract prose and keep the target/operation/anchor cites.

S5 (T014-T015) restates verifier prompt semantics and fail-category behavior (`required supporting quotations`, `three-fail-type discrimination`, `edge-local self-containment`) in the task text; that belongs in the spec, not the impl-plan wording.

S6 (T016-T019) embeds the derive/check/evaluate/results behavioral contract (`Deterministic projection`, `Pure-read totality gate`, `always returns success outcome`, cache/traversal semantics) directly in task prose, which is upstream restatement.
T022 restates CLI behavior and exit semantics (`No --lenient / --force / --context / --layer / --scope flags`, `results exit is always 0`) instead of staying at target + operation + anchor cite.
T023 restates capability-routing behavior (`fast → final escalation resolves per capability`) rather than just naming the config/registry edits and anchor cite.

T009's contract overstates the task text: it attributes `SemanticVerifierError`, `ArtifactCodecError`, `TestSourceScanError`, and `VerifyCacheError`, but the task description only names `ObligationCheckError`, `ObligationDeriveError`, `ObligationEvaluateError`, `ObligationResultsError`, `FulfillmentFailCategory`, and the port types. Either expand the task description to cover those entries or remove them from the contract.

T020's task-contract attributes `TestObligationDeriveInput`, `TestObligationCheckInput`, `TestObligationEvaluateInput`, and `TestObligationResultsInput`, but the T020 task description only names the four handler types and does not claim to add or modify these input entries. This is a task-contract attribution mismatch: an executor following the plan would not know those catalogue entries are part of T020.

T022's task-contract omits `TestObligationResultsArgs` even though the T022 task description explicitly lists `TestObligationResultsArgs` among the CLI args to add. That leaves a catalogue entry claimed by the task without task-contract attribution.

`AC-16` is mapped to `T014`, but `T014` only targets `test_obligation::fulfillment_verifier` provider wiring and its cited anchors are `IN-09/IN-12/CN-03/CN-08/AC-06/AC-08/OS-01`; it does not touch `trait_impls`, `contract_conformance`, or trait-edge evidence selection. This makes the `AC-16` coverage assignment implausible and misassigns load-bearing fulfillment-evaluation work away from the tasks that actually describe it.

`AC-11` is mapped to `T015`, but `T015` only adds the `WaiverVerifierAdapter` provider wiring. It does not target waiver-fail routing, preserving obligations without verifier-injected additions, or routing-brief handling, which are the load-bearing parts of `AC-11`; those are usecase/evaluate responsibilities already described by `T018`.

AC-12 is mapped to T016 and T017, but those task descriptions do not cite AC-12 or describe the derive/check work needed for voluntary bindings; only T018 carries the AC-12 cite. That makes the coverage mapping implausible for the derive/check portions of AC-12's transition path.

T004 restates upstream behavior in prose: `load-time totality verification and per-axis vocabulary parsing` plus the named fail cases duplicate AC-02/CN-05 details. Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, this should be target + operation + anchor cite only.

T010's test text restates the upstream identity/drift contract: `preserves TestObligationId identity when only declaration hash changes`. The impl-plan should cite IN-05/AC-03/CN-01 rather than restating that behavior.

T013 restates scanner/source-editing behavior in prose: locating tests by `(layer, module_path, test_name)`, extracting body spans, computing `TestBodySpanHash` without editing source, and whitespace stability. Those are upstream contract details covered by the cited anchors and should not be repeated here.

T023 restates AC-07's provider resolution behavior by spelling out `provider/model`, `fast_provider/fast_model`, and `RoundType::Fast` / `RoundType::Final` expectations. This violates the no-upstream-restatement convention for impl-plan task text.

T018 cites AC-07 and AC-08 and requires unit tests for those anchors, but task-coverage.json assigns AC-07 only to T023 and AC-08 only to T014. Those ACs cover capability registration / resolve_execution and fulfillment-verifier prompt calibration, while T018 targets the usecase evaluate interactor, so the plan gives T018 obligations that are not represented in coverage and are not executable at that target. Remove those citations from T018 or add explicit executable work plus matching coverage if the interactor must own them.

T001 is attributed to the usecase catalogue entry `SemanticEscalationFuture`, but the T001 plan text only instructs the executor to add `SemanticEscalationDriverPort`, `SemanticEscalationVerdictBridge`, and `SemanticCalibrationProbeConfig` plus tests. Under the impl-plan policy, task-contract entries must match entries the task actually describes touching; either add `SemanticEscalationFuture` to T001's executable description or remove this attribution.

T003's task-contract attribution list includes the new ValidationError bookkeeping entry but omits DomainError, even though the review briefing says both ValidationError and DomainError were added to T003 as required pre-review coverage-gate attribution. Leaving DomainError out keeps the task-contract SSoT incomplete for the Batch A attribution update.

T003 now attributes `ValidationError` in `task-contract.json`, but the T003 executable task text in `impl-plan.json`/`plan.md` still only names `TestObligationRulesLoadError` and `TestObligationRulesLoaderPort` for the errors/ports work. Because the plan never tells the executor to add or modify `ValidationError`, this attribution is not backed by the task description and can leave the catalogue entry unimplemented or implemented by guesswork.

T007 now attributes the domain catalogue entry `NonEmptyTestLocations` in `task-contract.json`, but the T007 task text in `impl-plan.json`/`plan.md` only adds `TestObligation`, `ObligationsDocument`, `TestLocation`, `TestBindingRecord`, `TestBindingsDocument`, `TestObligationScopePresence`, and `UncitedSpecElementFinding`. That makes the task-contract claim work that the executable task description does not touch, so the implementer has no plan instruction to add or verify `NonEmptyTestLocations`. Remove this attribution or add the entry explicitly to T007's task description and rendered plan.

The batch update in this round is on the wrong task set: the briefing says T010/T011/T012 should move to `in_progress`, but this plan marks T006/T007/T008/T009 as `done` and leaves T010-T012 untouched. That means the requested state transition is not reflected in the impl-plan, so the render in `plan.md` tracks the wrong batch.

Batch C was supposed to move T010/T011/T012 from `todo` to `in_progress`, but the plan still leaves T010 as `todo` here, with T011/T012 also still `todo` on the following task entries. As rendered in plan.md, this keeps the intended Batch C implementation tasks inactive rather than starting the correct batch.

T010's task-contract attribution includes `ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto`, but the T010 task description in `impl-plan.json`/rendered `plan.md` only instructs the implementer to add `CatalogueEntryRefDto` and never names or otherwise touches `ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto`. That leaves an attributed catalogue entry that the executable task does not actually cover; update the T010 description/rendered plan to include the `ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto` work or remove the attribution if it is not part of T010.

T010's description embeds the cleanup rationale in prose: "renamed from the earlier `CatalogueEntryRefDto` proposal after the short-name collision cleanup ... keeps its name ... `action: reference`, not re-added". Per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, impl-plan task text should stay to target + operation + anchor cite; carrying this rationale in `impl-plan.json` (and therefore rendered `plan.md`) creates a second source of truth for the DTO split instead of leaving that decision upstream.

`domain::tddd::test_obligation::ports::ObligationsArtifactPort` and `TestBindingsArtifactPort` expose `load`/`save` with `ObligationCheckError` / `ObligationDeriveError`, but these codec boundaries can only surface I/O / JSON / invariant failures. Variants such as `RulesLoad`, `CatalogueLoad`, `SpecLoad`, `InvalidCatalogueState`, `ObligationsAbsent`, `BindingsAbsent`, `PartialArtifactState`, `DriftsDetected`, `UnresolvedEdges`, and `StaleVerdicts` are not constructible at the port layer.

`domain::tddd::test_obligation::ports::ObligationFulfillmentCachePort`, `WaiverCachePort`, `ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort`, and `WaiverVerifierPort` all return `ObligationEvaluateError`, but the adapters behind those methods can only produce a narrow subset (`CachePersistence` for cache I/O, `VerifierPortError` for the LLM ports). Control-plane variants like `InvalidConfig`, `TrackNotActive`, `SemanticFailuresConfirmed`, and `HumanEscalationRequired` are not reachable from those methods.

`domain::tddd::test_obligation::ports::TestSourceScannerPort::scan_test_body` returns `ObligationCheckError`, but the scanner can only fail on I/O / parse / missing-test conditions. Higher-level check outcomes such as `ObligationsAbsent`, `BindingsAbsent`, `PartialArtifactState`, `DriftsDetected`, `UnresolvedEdges`, and `StaleVerdicts` are not constructible from that boundary.

Ownership smell: `ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort::verify_pair` takes `tests_source`, `entry_declaration`, and `anchor_text` as owned `String`s even though the port is read-only and could borrow `&str`; this forces avoidable allocation/cloning at the usecase boundary.

Ownership smell: `WaiverVerifierPort::verify_pair` takes `waived_reason`, `entry_declaration`, and `anchor_text` as owned `String`s even though the port is read-only and could borrow `&str`; this forces avoidable allocation/cloning at the usecase boundary.

Lossy boundary downgrade: `ObligationCheckError::DriftsDetected`, `UnresolvedEdges`, and `StaleVerdicts` collapse structured failure data into counts, while `CheckTestObligationsOutcome` already carries the full `Vec<TestObligationDrift>`, `Vec<TestObligationEdgeId>`, and `Vec<UncitedSpecElementFinding>`; the error shape drops actionable detail without justification.

`test_obligation::evaluate::TestObligationEvaluateConfig::try_new` returns `ObligationEvaluateError`, but this constructor can only reject invalid config values. Callers still have to handle `TrackNotActive`, `VerifierPort`, `CachePersistence`, `SemanticFailuresConfirmed`, and `HumanEscalationRequired`, none of which are reachable at this boundary. Narrow the error type or document why the full enum is intentional.

`semantic_verdict_core::driver::SemanticEscalationDriverPort::evaluate_with_escalation` also returns `ObligationEvaluateError`, but the method only takes `key` and `initial_tier`. The config-only and track-only variants (`InvalidConfig`, `TrackNotActive`) are not structurally reachable here, so the shared error enum is broader than the port boundary warrants unless the catalogue explains that reuse.

`ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort::verify_pair` and `WaiverVerifierPort::verify_pair` are synchronous `&self` methods even though both docs describe dispatching to LLM capabilities. That hides blocking external I/O behind a sync boundary without any justification in the catalogue; make the ports async or explicitly document the blocking choice.

Track-active guard ownership is split across layers. The cli_driver DTOs for derive/check/evaluate say the handler enforces `track/<id>` before translation, while `DeriveTestObligationsCommand` and `CheckTestObligationsCommand` say the interactor rejects on the guard even though `ObligationDeriveError` and `ObligationCheckError` have no `TrackNotActive` variant. That leaves no single owner for the rule, and the derive/check error contracts cannot carry the rejection data they claim to produce.

`SemanticEscalationDriverPort::evaluate_with_escalation` is declared as the responsibility-neutral D7 core shared by ref-verify and the test-obligation lanes, but its error type is `domain::tddd::test_obligation::errors::ObligationEvaluateError`. That forces non-obligation callers of the shared core to handle obligation-only variants such as `InvalidConfig` and `TrackNotActive`, and the method docs only narrow the subset instead of making the type precise. Use a neutral core error or associated error and map it to `ObligationEvaluateError` at the evaluate interactor boundary.

`ObligationCheckError` includes `VerifierPort(SemanticVerifierError)`, but `check` is specified and catalogued as pure-read with no LLM/verifier execution, and `CheckTestObligationsInteractor::new` does not receive either verifier port. This leaves an unconstructible check error variant and makes `CheckTestObligationsApplicationService::execute` callers handle a failure mode the operation cannot structurally produce.

`SemanticEscalationDriverPort::evaluate_with_escalation` claims to run a verification pair, but its signature only accepts `key: K` and `initial_tier`; the documented `K` is the per-verifier cache key, and the declared cache keys are hash tuples, not the claim/evidence text needed by the fulfillment, waiver, or ref-verify verifier ports. As written, a conforming implementation cannot perform the documented verification without relying on hidden state not represented by the contract.

`ObligationFulfillmentCachePort`, `ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort`, `TestSourceScannerPort`, `WaiverCachePort`, and `WaiverVerifierPort` are declared as domain-layer `SecondaryPort`s even though their docs describe verify-cache file I/O, syn-based source scanning, and LLM capability invocation. Per `knowledge/conventions/hexagonal-architecture.md` Port Placement Rules, infrastructure capabilities that are not domain concepts belong behind usecase ports; keeping them in `domain::tddd::test_obligation::ports` makes the inner layer own application/provider/cache/scanner abstractions and their adapter-fault vocabulary.

`ObligationCheckError::PartialArtifactState(TestObligationScopePresence)` accepts the full scope enum even though `TestObligationScopePresence` documents `Both` as gate evaluation and `Neither` as zero-pair pass; only `ObligationsOnly` and `BindingsOnly` are partial fail-closed states. This payload shape makes impossible error states representable, and the sibling `ObligationsAbsent` / `BindingsAbsent` variants further blur which state owns the rejection.

`TestObligationDrift::new` takes independent `Option<TestObligationId>` and `Option<TestObligationEdgeId>` parameters while the entry describes each drift as targeting a single obligation or edge. The contract admits `None/None` drifts with no target and `Some/Some` drifts with two targets, so the drift kind-to-target invariant is not represented in the type shape.

`ObligationEvaluateError::SemanticFailuresConfirmed` and `HumanEscalationRequired` collapse the failed/pending evaluation set to `pair_count`, while the sibling results path carries typed `Vec<EdgeVerdictRecord>` detail records. The evaluate gate has the edge/pair identities at the failure point, but this error contract discards them without a documented justification, leaving callers unable to report or route the exact failed edges from the failing command.

`TestObligation` is constructed with `target_role`, `declaration_hash`, and `spec_refs`, but its public surface only exposes `id`, `target_entry`, and `brief` while the fields are stripped/private. The check/evaluate usecases need those values to derive edge coverage and cache keys, so the domain contract makes required cross-layer data unobservable outside the domain crate.

`TestObligationRulesDocument::try_new` accepts `function_roles`, `patterns`, and `trait_impls`, but the public accessors expose only `data_roles` and `contract_roles` while the fields are stripped/private. IN-03 requires derive to apply all five rule sections, so the usecase layer cannot consume the complete validated rules document through the declared contract.

`ObligationFulfillmentVerifierPort`, `WaiverVerifierPort`, and `TestSourceScannerPort` are declared as domain-layer `SecondaryPort`s even though their docs describe LLM capability invocation and source parsing/materialization. Per `knowledge/conventions/hexagonal-architecture.md` Port Placement Rules, infrastructure capabilities needed by application services belong behind usecase ports, not in the inner domain layer.

`CheckTestObligationsOutcome::new` accepts the full `TestObligationScopePresence`, but `ObligationsOnly` and `BindingsOnly` are fail-closed states modeled as `ObligationCheckError` variants. This permits an `Ok(CheckTestObligationsOutcome)` to carry a partial-artifact failure state, so the success DTO admits an illegal state. Use a success-only presence type or constructors that cannot encode the partial states.

`TestObligationDrift` takes an unconstrained `TestObligationDriftKind` in both `new_obligation` and `new_edge`, even though the six drift kinds have different origins/targets. The contract can construct nonsensical combinations such as an obligation-targeted `ReasonChanged` drift or an edge-targeted `Missing` drift. Split the target-specific drift shapes or expose constructors per valid drift family so invalid kind/target pairs are unrepresentable.

The artifact save methods return read-side codec errors. For example, `ObligationsArtifactPort::save(&ObligationsDocument)` returns `ArtifactCodecError`, whose variants include `MalformedJson` and `DomainInvariant` during `into_domain`; saving an already-validated domain document cannot produce those variants, and the method docs do not state a producible subset or justify the broad enum. The same issue applies to `TestBindingsArtifactPort::save` and the cache `save` methods with `VerifyCacheError`, forcing callers to handle impossible failures.

`SemanticEscalationDriverPort::evaluate_with_escalation` is declared synchronous while the docs describe verifier adapter failures, cache persistence, and fast/final/human escalation through capability-backed verification. That method set implies external I/O, but unlike the domain verifier ports this entry does not acknowledge or justify the synchronous color, so the catalogue can lock adapters into a blocking API unexpectedly.

`ObligationsCodecError` and `TestBindingsCodecError` duplicate the same error contract already declared as domain `ArtifactCodecError`: all three expose `Io`, `MalformedJson`, and `DomainInvariant` variants carrying `DiagnosticMessage`, and the bindings error is explicitly documented as a mirror. This is duplicated structural declaration across neighbouring layers without one entry being a reference to the shared contract, so any codec error-shape change now has to be made in three catalogue entries instead of the port-boundary error being the SSoT.

`domain-types.json` has multiple `docs` fields that restate upstream behavior instead of only citing the relevant anchors. Examples include `ArtifactCodecError` spelling out load/save failure-mode behavior, `ObligationCheckError` restating partial-artifact and staleness recovery semantics, `ObligationFulfillmentCacheKey` / `WaiverCacheKey` restating CN-04 invalidation/recovery rules, `ObligationFulfillmentVerdict` / `WaiverVerdict` restating citation and pending-fails-gate behavior, `TestObligationRulesDocument` / `TestObligationRulesLoadError` restating CN-05 totality requirements, `TestObligationScopePresence` restating AC-10 scope outcomes, `VerifyCacheError` restating fail-closed cache semantics, and `ObligationResultsError` restating results exit behavior. This violates `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`; these docs should be reduced to type purpose plus anchor cites.

`usecase-types.json` repeats behavioral contract text in catalogue docs rather than deferring to anchors. `CheckTestObligationsApplicationService`, `EvaluateTestObligationsApplicationService`, `TestObligationResultsApplicationService`, `CheckTestObligationsInteractor`, `CheckTestObligationsOutcome`, `EvaluateTestObligationsOutcome`, `TestObligationResultsCommand`, and `TestObligationResultsInteractor` restate pure-read/fail-closed, escalation/cache, branch-guard, calibration, and exit-code rules from the spec. Per the no-upstream-restatement convention, these should reference the anchors without re-describing the behavior.

Infrastructure catalogue docs restate upstream behavior across adapter entries. `JsonObligationsCodec` restates atomic write and absent-file behavior, `JsonTestBindingsCodec` restates production write ownership, `JsonTestObligationRulesLoader` restates load-time totality validation, `ObligationFulfillmentVerifierAdapter` / `WaiverVerifierAdapter` restate capability-resolution and escalation details, `SynTestSourceScanner` restates scanner behavior, and `TestObligationRulesDocumentDto` restates total map decoding / fail-closed behavior. These are behavioral contracts that belong behind spec/ADR anchors, not duplicated in `<layer>-types.json` docs.

The CLI catalogue docs restate the CLI behavior contract. `TestObligationArgs` restates the no `--lenient` / `--force` / scope-flag rule, the per-subcommand arg entries restate branch-resolution behavior, and `TestObligationSubcommand` restates the closed command set and extension policy. These should be anchor-only references under the no-upstream-restatement convention.

The CLI driver catalogue docs restate presentation behavior from the spec. `TestObligationCheckHandler` restates rendered failure categories and fail-closed exit behavior, `TestObligationResultsHandler` restates result block structure and exit code, and `TestObligationResultsInput` restates the no-branch-guard/read-only viewer rule. These duplicate upstream behavior instead of citing anchors.

`TestObligationCompositionRoot` docs restate provider/capability resolution behavior from upstream (`agent-profiles.json` / resolve_execution path). The catalogue entry should cite the relevant anchors and avoid reproducing that behavior contract in prose.

`TestObligationRulesDocument::try_new` takes already-typed `BTreeMap<...>` inputs but returns the full `TestObligationRulesLoadError` loader enum. That enum includes variants such as `IoError`, `MalformedJson`, and `UnknownRoleName` that this constructor cannot structurally produce after parsing and key conversion have already happened, forcing constructor callers to handle unreachable loader failures. Narrow this constructor's error type or document the producible subset.

`TestObligationEvaluateConfig::try_new` validates only `injection_rate`, `detection_threshold`, and `parallelism`, but returns the full `ObligationEvaluateError` enum. Besides `InvalidConfig`, that enum includes runtime failures like `TrackNotActive`, verifier/cache failures, and semantic escalation outcomes, none of which can be produced by this value-object constructor. Use a narrower config validation error or explicitly document the reachable subset.

`TestObligationRulesDocument::try_new` exposes `BTreeMap<DataRole, ...>`, `BTreeMap<ContractRole, ...>`, `BTreeMap<FunctionRole, ...>`, and `BTreeMap<TestObligationPatternKind, ...>` in its public contract, but those key types are not declared as `Ord` in this catalogue/baseline. `BTreeMap<K, _>` requires `K: Ord`, so implementing this shape either fails to compile or requires undeclared modify entries on the role/key enums. Use an ordered key type that has the required bound, or declare the companion type modifications explicitly.

`TestObligationRulesDocument::try_new` claims `ObligationsFieldOmitted` is a producible error, but its inputs receive already-constructed `RoleObligationRules` values, and `RoleObligationRules::new` only accepts `Vec<TestObligationRule>`. At that point the JSON distinction between an omitted `obligations` field and an explicit empty `obligations: []` has been erased, so the domain constructor cannot own the AC-02/CN-05 fail-closed check it claims. Preserve field-presence in the type shape or make the DTO/loader the sole declared owner of this rejection.

`SemanticCalibrationProbeConfig` is declared inside the responsibility-neutral `semantic_verdict_core::probe`, but its constructor takes `RefVerifyPercent` for both calibration values. `RefVerifyPercent` is ref-verify-specific vocabulary, so the shared semantic-verdict core would force the test-obligation gate and any later verifier to depend on ref-verify’s type contract instead of a neutral percent/config type. That contradicts the IN-01/AC-15 boundary that keeps verifier-specific pieces outside the shared core.

`SemanticEscalationVerdictBridge` hard-codes the current verifier lanes (`Fulfillment`, `Waiver`, `RefVerify`) and carries their concrete verifier-specific verdict payloads inside `semantic_verdict_core`. A responsibility-neutral core should not need a new enum variant every time another semantic verifier is added; the existing generic `SemanticEscalationDriverPort<P, K, V, E>` already lets `V` remain verifier-owned. As catalogued, this is a closed extension point in the shared core and leaks verifier-specific types across the boundary required by IN-01/AC-15.

`CatalogueEntryRefDto` is being added as a new infrastructure DTO for `domain::tddd::semantic_verify::CatalogueEntryRef`, but the infrastructure layer already has the same-purpose DTO in `tddd::semantic_verify_codec`. This duplicates the wire-shape SSoT for catalogue entry references instead of reusing or declaring a reference to the existing DTO, so future changes to `CatalogueEntryRef` can diverge between semantic-verify and test-obligation codecs.

`ValidationError.docs` restates upstream rationale and rollout state instead of acting as a catalog anchor: it explains that this track adds `InvalidObligationMinimum(usize)` to support `TestObligationMinimum`, and even describes the Yellow signal / pre-review gate posture. In `<layer>-types.json`, this field should reference the upstream anchor, not reproduce the briefing narrative.

`core::convert::From<ValidationError>` for `DomainError` is marked `modify`, but the only branch change here is the new `ValidationError::InvalidObligationMinimum` variant; the `DomainError` conversion impl itself is unchanged. This overstates the diff and should be `reference`/omitted, as in the same pattern on prior tracks.
`SemanticEscalationFuture`'s docs explain the object-safety/worker-task rationale instead of just anchoring the contract, which is an upstream restatement in the type catalogue.
`SemanticEscalationDriverPort` over-constrains `V` and `E` with `Sync`; the boxed `Send` future only needs them to be `Send`, so this rejects valid implementors without adding safety.

`SemanticEscalationFuture` is missing the borrow lifetime from the source alias. In `libs/usecase/src/semantic_verdict_core/driver.rs` the alias is `SemanticEscalationFuture<'a, V, E>`, but this catalogue entry only records `V` and `E`, and the port method below it returns `SemanticEscalationFuture<'_, V, E>` without any lifetime parameter in the contract. That makes the type contract incomplete and can mislead consumers about the future's borrow relationship to `&self` / the inputs.

`SemanticEscalationDriverPort` is under-specified in the catalogue: [`usecase-types.json`]( /home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/track/items/test-obligation-fulfillment-gate-2026-07-07/usecase-types.json ) records `P`/`K` as `Send + Sync`, but it only records `V`/`E` as `Send`. The implementation at [`libs/usecase/src/semantic_verdict_core/driver.rs`]( /home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/libs/usecase/src/semantic_verdict_core/driver.rs#L28-L33 ) requires `V`/`E: Send + Sync` as well, so the published port contract is too permissive and would admit non-Sync verdict/error types that cannot actually implement the trait.

`DomainError` now exposes a `Transition` arm whose payload is `TransitionError`, but none of the reviewed type catalogues declare `TransitionError` as a tracked type. The source definition exists at [`libs/domain/src/error.rs`]( /home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/libs/domain/src/error.rs#L104-L110 ), yet the catalogue and contract map never surface the payload type, so `DomainError::Transition` is only partially representable in the type SSoT.

`domain::error::DomainError`'s docs field explains the rationale for keeping this entry as a reference instead of just anchoring the change to IN-02/T003. That prose restates upstream design intent in a `docs` field, which the no-upstream-restatement convention forbids for `<layer>-types.json` entries.

P1: [`domain-types.json`](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/track/items/test-obligation-fulfillment-gate-2026-07-07/domain-types.json#L4488-L4504) narrows `ValidationError` to only `InvalidObligationMinimum(usize)`, but the same file still exposes multiple public `try_new` constructors that return `Result<_, ValidationError>` for unrelated text/newtype validation, e.g. [`RoleName::try_new`](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/track/items/test-obligation-fulfillment-gate-2026-07-07/domain-types.json#L2528-L2555), [`TestObligationBrief::try_new`](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/track/items/test-obligation-fulfillment-gate-2026-07-07/domain-types.json#L3273-L3297), [`TestObligationAnchorId::try_new`](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/track/items/test-obligation-fulfillment-gate-2026-07-07/domain-types.json#L3216-L3243), and [`WaivedReason::try_new`](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/track/items/test-obligation-fulfillment-gate-2026-07-07/domain-types.json#L4565-L4588). Those constructors cannot structurally produce the only remaining variant, so callers are forced to handle an impossible branch and the failure space for those APIs is no longer represented.

`domain::ValidationError` is catalogued as if every pre-existing data-carrying variant were unit-shaped, but the real enum in [`libs/domain/src/error.rs`](file:///home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/libs/domain/src/error.rs#L16) has payloads for variants such as `InvalidTrackId(String)`, `BranchIdMismatch { .. }`, `StatusOverrideMismatch { .. }`, `TrackActivationRequiresPlanningOnly { .. }`, `TrackActivationRequiresSchemaV3 { .. }`, `TrackAlreadyMaterialized { .. }`, `TaskDescriptionMutated { .. }`, and `TaskRemoved { .. }`. That strips the public contract down to an incorrect shape and would mislead downstream consumers.

`DomainError` is marked `reference`, but the catalogue is not baseline-identical: it only declares `From<ValidationError>` and omits the rustdoc-visible `Debug`, `Error`, and `From<TransitionError>` impls from `libs/domain/src/error.rs`. Because `TransitionError` has no type entry anywhere in this scope, the `Transition` arm's payload is invisible to the type SSoT.

`ValidationError` is catalogued with `unit` payloads for variants that are payload-bearing in the real domain enum (`libs/domain/src/error.rs:16`), for example `InvalidTrackId`, `BranchIdMismatch`, `StatusOverrideMismatch`, `TrackActivationRequiresPlanningOnly`, `TrackActivationRequiresSchemaV3`, `TrackAlreadyMaterialized`, `TaskDescriptionMutated`, and `TaskRemoved`. That makes the domain type contract lossy and incorrect for downstream consumers.

`DomainError::Transition(TransitionError)` is only half-catalogued here: this scope adds the enum arm, but it never declares a `TransitionError` type entry, so the payload is dead vocabulary for catalog consumers. The source enum exposes that branch, but the type SSoT in this PR cannot represent it.

`JsonTestObligationRulesLoader::new` is catalogued with only `config_path: PathBuf`, but the implementation also requires `trusted_root: PathBuf` and stores it for path-guarding. That leaves the new adapter contract incomplete and inconsistent with the actual public API (`libs/infrastructure/src/test_obligation/rules_codec.rs:207`).

`TestObligationRulesLoaderPort` is a synchronous secondary port for loading the test-obligation rules document, but its entry docs no longer acknowledge the sync choice. The port name/spec refs imply config/file I/O (`.harness/config/test-obligation-rules.json` via IN-02/IN-04), so the type contract should keep the sync rationale in the catalogue docs to avoid a sync/async color ambiguity at the adapter boundary.

`NonEmptyTestLocations` restates upstream behavior in its catalogue docs instead of limiting the type entry to the local declaration plus anchor cites. The entry explains the Fulfillment/VoluntaryBinding non-empty binding rule, the `JsonTestBindingsCodec` fail-closed boundary behavior, and the rationale for replacing `Vec<TestLocation>`; those are IN-06/AC-04/AC-12/D9 behavioral decisions and belong in the upstream spec/ADR per `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`. Keeping that prose here creates a second source of truth if the binding semantics change.

Batch C's round-trip contract is not represented for the T004 rules DTOs. The trait_impls block declares only `serde_core::de::Deserialize<'de>` for `TestObligationPerAxisDto`, `TestObligationRuleDto`, `RoleObligationRulesDto`, and `TestObligationRulesDocumentDto`, with no matching `serde_core::ser::Serialize` entries. The briefing requires Serialize for those four existing DTOs, so the type catalogue omits the post-change API surface that makes the rules artifact round-trip-ready.

`domain::ValidationError`'s `docs` field is change-log prose, not a contract note: it narrates the `String -> DiagnosticMessage` refactor, mentions `T006`, and defers work to an implementer follow-up. The catalog should just anchor the contract and avoid restating upstream rationale.

`test_obligation::obligations_codec::ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto`'s `docs` field does the same thing: it explains the alias split and evaluator symbol-disambiguation rationale in prose instead of staying at the catalog-contract level. That violates the no-upstream-restatement rule for `docs` / `intent` fields.

`CatalogueEntryRefDto` is added as a public DTO, but this catalog entry records no inherent methods even though the implementation now exposes `from_domain` and `into_domain`. That leaves the post-change API shape incomplete in the type SSoT.

Both `ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto::into_domain` and `CatalogueEntryRefDto::into_domain` expose `domain::ValidationError`, but the only structurally reachable failure is `ValidationError::EmptyString` from `CatalogueEntryKey::try_new`; the other 35 variants are impossible at this boundary. Narrow the return type or document why callers must handle the whole enum.

`CatalogueEntryRefDto` is the preexisting `semantic_verify_codec` DTO, so this entry should not be `action: add`. The source type is still a serde wire DTO, but the catalog now treats it as a brand-new struct and only lists `Debug`/`Clone`/`PartialEq`/`Eq`, dropping the `Serialize` / `Deserialize` trait_impls that the Rust code derives.

`test_obligation::obligations_codec::ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto` is a structural duplicate of `tddd::semantic_verify_codec::CatalogueEntryRefDto`: same empty DTO shape, same `from_domain`/`into_domain` signatures, and the same `CatalogueEntryRef` validation path. Because the catalogue does not declare a `reference` relation between them, the same wire contract now has to be maintained in two places (also mirrored in `contract-map.md`).

`ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto`'s `docs` field restates the duplication rationale in prose ('independent struct', 'genuine local type', 'contract, not type reuse') instead of staying at the contract level. The accepted duplicate itself is fine; the docs field should not become a second source of truth for that decision.

`ObligationCatalogueEntryRefDto::into_domain` and `CatalogueEntryRefDto::into_domain` both expose the full `domain::ValidationError` enum even though the only reachable failure is `ValidationError::EmptyString` from `CatalogueEntryKey::try_new`. That leaves the rest of the enum as dead vocabulary at this boundary without justification.

`infrastructure::track::fs_store::load_impl_plan_for_track` is catalogued as `Result<Option<domain::ImplPlanDocument>, domain::RepositoryError>`, but the implementation at `/home/flip451/individual/t-rust/templates/SoTOHE-core-002/libs/infrastructure/src/track/fs_store.rs:475` returns `Option<ImplPlanDocument>` and swallows all failures with `ok()?`. The catalog advertises an error path that cannot actually occur.

`tddd::semantic_verify_codec::CatalogueEntryRefDto` is a preexisting cross-track DTO, but this catalog entry is marked `action: add` and its serde trait impls are also recorded as `add`. The branch is claiming a new API surface here instead of referencing the existing type, so the type SSoT overstates the diff.

The `docs` field for `infrastructure::track::fs_store::load_impl_plan_for_track` restates the helper's behavior and rationale (`None` on any failure, render-only helper for the T013 hardening path) instead of keeping the catalog entry to target + operation + anchor cite. That violates the no-upstream-restatement rule for `<layer>-types.json` docs.

`CatalogueEntryRefDto` is catalogued as `action: add`, but this is the preexisting shared DTO in `tddd::semantic_verify_codec` that the track plan says to reference. The associated serde impls on the same surface are also marked `add`; they should be `reference` entries so the catalog reflects reuse rather than a new public type.

`infrastructure::track::fs_store::load_impl_plan_for_track` is tied to `CN-14`, but that spec item is about test-source body handling and artifact-side hashes, not impl-plan loading. The anchor is off-topic for this helper, so the traceability link is misleading.

`tddd::semantic_verify_codec::CatalogueEntryRefDto` is a preexisting cross-track DTO: the underlying Rust source in `libs/infrastructure/src/tddd/semantic_verify_codec.rs` is unchanged in this PR. This catalogue entry should therefore be `action: reference`, not `add`, and the attached `core::fmt::Debug` / `Clone` / `Eq` / `PartialEq` / `Serialize` / `Deserialize` rows should be `reference` as well; otherwise the track falsely claims ownership of an unchanged type.

`JsonTestObligationRulesLoader::load` reads `config_path` with `read_to_string` but never rejects symlinks. That means a symlinked `test-obligation-rules.json` will be followed to its target instead of enforcing real-file semantics, unlike the other config loaders in this repo that `symlink_metadata()` and fail closed before reading.

This guard only rejects symlinks; it never canonicalizes or verifies that `config_path` stays within a fixed trusted root. A non-symlink path with `..` components can therefore escape the expected `.harness/config` boundary and be read directly. The existing `scope_config_loader.rs` pattern canonicalizes the root/path and `starts_with`-checks containment before reading.

`JsonTestObligationRulesLoader` does not anchor its trust boundary to an external `trusted_root`. When `.harness/config` is absent, `infer_symlink_trusted_root` and `infer_config_boundary_root` both fall back to `config_path.parent()`, so the containment check at `guard_config_path` becomes tautological and the adapter will read arbitrary files or files under a symlinked directory if the leaf itself is not a symlink. This is a trusted-root violation; compare the explicit `trusted_root` + canonicalize pattern used by `load_v2_scope_config` in `review_v2/scope_config_loader.rs`.

`reject_symlinks_below` treats its second argument as an already-trusted root and does not stat it. This codec passes `items_dir` as that root without first rejecting a symlinked `items_dir`, so constructing the adapter with `track/items` as a symlink lets `load` read through the symlink and `save` create/write under the symlink target outside the intended workspace boundary. Mirror the existing trusted-root pattern by checking the root itself before using it as the guard root.

`reject_symlinks_below` assumes `items_dir` is already a safe trusted root, but this adapter never checks that root. A symlinked `items_dir` is therefore accepted, and the subsequent `read_to_string`/`write` operations follow it outside the intended artifact tree. Reject a symlinked root before joining track artifacts beneath it.

The fulfillment cache guard checks components below `items_dir`, but not `items_dir` itself. Because `read_to_string` and `write` follow symlinks, a symlinked cache root can redirect cache I/O outside the trusted track items directory. Add an explicit root symlink rejection before using `items_dir` as the guard root.

The waiver cache adapter uses `items_dir` as the trusted root for `reject_symlinks_below` without validating that root. If `items_dir` is a symlink, the guard stops before inspecting it and the cache load/save follows the symlink target, violating the real-file boundary convention. Reject symlinked roots before artifact path resolution.

`location.module_path()` is split into `crate_name`/`rest` and both are concatenated into `workspace_root/...` with `join`/`push` but no containment check against `workspace_root`. A crafted module path containing `..` or an absolute component can escape the worktree before `read_to_string` runs.

`std::fs::read_to_string(&file)` will follow symlinks, but this scanner never does a `symlink_metadata()`/reject check on candidate files or the workspace root. That means a symlinked test source under the worktree is accepted instead of being fail-closed.

`guarded_workspace_root()` canonicalizes the caller-supplied workspace root after only checking the final path component for symlinks. That can follow symlinked ancestor components and re-anchor the scanner on the target tree, which violates the trusted-root boundary. The existing `verify/trusted_root.rs` pattern keeps the root lexical and only rejects a symlinked root instead of calling `canonicalize()` here.

`guarded_workspace_root()` only `symlink_metadata()`-checks the leaf `workspace_root` path. If the repo is reached through a symlinked parent such as `/tmp/link/repo`, this passes, and the later `reject_symlinks_below()` calls treat that untrusted anchor as the trusted root. That leaves the scanner able to read from a redirected tree instead of rejecting the symlink boundary, which is the case the trusted-root / symlink-guard precedent in `verify/trusted_root.rs` is meant to block.

`read_track_metadata` and `load_impl_plan_for_track` still call `std::fs::read_to_string` on `items_dir.join(id)` paths without the `symlink_metadata` / `reject_symlinks_below` guard that `read_track_status_str` applies. A symlinked `items_dir` or track directory will be followed and can read outside the trusted root, so these public helpers do not fail closed at the filesystem boundary.

`guarded_items_dir()` canonicalizes `items_dir` lexically before any containment check, so a path like `.../link/../items` can hide a symlinked component from `reject_symlinked_items_dir_chain()` and be re-anchored outside the intended track tree. `read_track_metadata()` / `load_impl_plan_for_track()` then trust that escaped directory as the root; this needs the same fail-closed `ParentDir`/containment guard used by the existing symlink-safe loaders.

`FsTrackStore` still builds primary port paths with raw `self.root.join(...).join(...)` and then calls `path.exists()`/`std::fs::read_to_string` without rejecting symlinks. `ImplPlanReader::load_impl_plan` repeats the same pattern for `impl-plan.json`, so callers of `TrackReader::find` / `ImplPlanReader::load_impl_plan` can follow a symlinked track directory or leaf file under the configured items root. Route these reads through the same trusted-root and `reject_symlinks_below` guard used by `read_track_metadata` / `guarded_track_file_path`.

`save_impl_plan` still builds the write target with `self.root.join(id.as_ref()).join("impl-plan.json")` and writes via `atomic_write_file` without first applying the same trusted-root/symlink guard used by the read paths. A symlinked `items_dir` or track directory can therefore redirect the impl-plan write outside the intended track-items root; this should fail closed via the existing `guarded_items_dir`/`reject_symlinks_below` pattern before creating the parent or temp file.

`with_locked_document` derives `metadata.json.lock` from a guarded metadata path, but then opens the lock with `std::fs::File::create` without checking the lock path itself for symlinks. A pre-existing symlink at `<track>/metadata.json.lock` will be followed and truncated before the lock is taken, bypassing the symlink-rejection boundary used elsewhere and conflicting with the scope_config_loader.rs symlink-rejection precedent. Guard `lock_path` with `reject_symlinks_below` or equivalent no-follow semantics before creating it.

`TestObligationRulesLoaderPort` is a domain-owned trait for loading `.harness/config/test-obligation-rules.json` from a configured source and reporting I/O / malformed JSON failures. That abstracts an infrastructure/application capability, while `knowledge/conventions/hexagonal-architecture.md` §Port Placement Rules says ports for infrastructure functions belong in `usecase`, with domain ports reserved for domain concepts such as persistence/worktree state. Keeping this loader in `libs/domain` misplaces the port boundary for the derivation/check use cases.

`TargetEntryRoleKind` does not make the role-section invariant unrepresentable: each section variant accepts the global `RoleKind`, so callers can construct invalid states such as `TargetEntryRoleKind::DataRole(RoleKind::Repository)` or `ContractRole(RoleKind::ValueObject)`. Because this is public domain API and there is no validating constructor or narrower per-section role type, downstream rule lookup can receive a target whose outer section and inner role disagree. This violates the domain enum/type-safety intent from `prefer-type-safe-abstractions.md` §Enum-first; use section-specific payloads or otherwise prevent mismatched construction.

`TestBindingRecord::Fulfillment` and `VoluntaryBinding` expose raw `Vec<TestLocation>` fields, so callers can construct a binding with `tests: vec![]`. That makes an obligation look bound while carrying no executable test evidence, undermining IN-06/AC-04's fail-closed binding check. Use a non-empty test-location collection newtype or private variants plus validating constructors so empty bindings are unrepresentable.

`TestBindingRecord` stores bound tests as a raw `Vec<TestLocation>` for fulfillment/voluntary bindings, with no non-empty value object or fallible constructor. The variant docs define these records as binding tests, but the domain type can still represent an empty test set, so the obligation gate can no longer rely on the type to distinguish a real test binding from no evidence. Encode the non-empty bound-test-set invariant in the type or constructor.

`NonEmptyTestLocations::first` uses production index access (`&self.0[0]`). The domain severity policy classifies index access outside `#[cfg(test)]` as panic-able library code under `coding-principles.md` §No Panics in Library Code; this method should avoid a panic-capable indexing operation even though constructors intend to preserve the non-empty invariant.

`SemanticEscalationDriverPort` is the shared escalation/cache port for concurrent semantic evaluation, but the trait leaves `P`, `K`, `V`, `E`, and the future produced by the public `async fn` unconstrained. A non-`Send`/non-`Sync` implementation can satisfy this usecase port, so later ref-verify or obligation-gate orchestration cannot safely fan out evaluations across workers despite the port contract being the concurrency boundary. Add the required `Send`/`Sync` bounds and use a `Send` future shape at the trait boundary instead of an unconstrained public `async fn`.
findings.category: purity violation by trait or generic

findings.message: D9 makes `anchor id` part of the obligation id, but D2 explicitly says obligations are derived per entry and are not multiplied by cite count. Downstream derivation cannot know whether to emit one obligation per declaration item, reusing its test group across all cited anchors, or one obligation per `(entry, anchor, kind, item)`. That changes obligation counts, binding shape, and totality semantics, so the ADR needs one consistent identity model before spec/types can translate it.
